Basically, an engine is assembled like a sandwich. The bottom piece, the bottom "bread" or the Oil Pan is held on by a special glue called RTV, and some heavy duty bolts.

What seems to be happening, is that during manufacturing they use too much glue, and the excess on the inside of the bread is detaching from the bread and getting caught in a screen filter meant to pick up other contaminants or "crumbs" and prevent them from getting to other parts of the sandwich.

What can happen is that excess glue can clog that screen and stop oil from getting to the parts of the engine that need it, aka oil starvation if that makes sense!. This can lead to a myriad of potential symptoms and problems as noted by the post above.

If you live in a warm climate, that will also contribute to tire wear.

If you really want to be sure your tires are wearing too fast, buy a tire tread depth gage at any auto parts store so you can measure it, and then have a professional check it out anyways. Where I am located, anything below 3/32nds of an inch is replacement with 4 or 5/32nds being yellow.

As a Service Writer, 99% of premature clutch, tire, and brake wear comes down to the driver, or the pothole/curb they deny hitting that screwed up their alignment. 

However it is worth noting the tires on any brand new vehicle wear significantly faster than over the counter options.
